summary: Announces that the Haskins Laboratory Very Distant Host connection would move from BBN's IMP to Harvard's IMP, changing the Host's network address from 197 to 201 while its host number stayed the same.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 634 announces a planned move of the Haskins Laboratory host connection from BBN to Harvard. The host number stays 3, but its network address changes from 197 to 201.

questions: what was the new haskins laboratory address
subtitle: A planned move of the Haskins Laboratory host connection changes its network address.

tldr.problem: The Haskins Laboratory Very Distant Host connection was planned to move from BBN's IMP to Harvard's IMP.
tldr.mechanism: The host number remains 3 while its network address changes from 197 to 201 to reflect the new connection point.
tldr.outcome: The move was expected sometime between May 8 and May 22, probably toward the end of that period, but its exact date depended on new telephone-company circuits.

today: The unit records RFC 634's status as Unknown and lists no updates or obsoleting RFCs. The RFC is a notice of a planned historical address change for the Haskins Laboratory host.

sections.title: The New Haskins Laboratory Address
sections.content:
The Haskins Laboratory Very Distant Host connection was expected to move from BBN, IMP 5, to Harvard, IMP 9. The host number remains Host 3, but its network address changes from 197 to 201.

The RFC does not give a precise move date. It expects the change sometime between May 8 and May 22, probably toward the end of that period.
sections.plainLanguage: The Haskins host was scheduled to connect through Harvard instead of BBN. Its host number stays the same, while its network address changes.

sections.title: Why the Date Was Uncertain
sections.content:
The exact date depended on the local telephone company installing new circuits. Because that work determined when the connection could move, the author could not provide a more precise date.

The memo announces the planned address change and the expected date window; it does not say when the move was ultimately completed.
sections.plainLanguage: The connection could move only after new telephone circuits were installed. The RFC gives an expected time window but does not confirm the final date.

sections.title: What the Notice Confirms
sections.content:
The RFC states that the Host number remains 3 while the network address changes from 197 to 201 as the connection moves from BBN IMP 5 to Harvard IMP 9.

It is a notice of a future change, with its timing dependent on circuit installation. It does not report a completed move.
sections.plainLanguage: The notice gives the new address and the IMP connection it is meant to identify. It does not confirm that the planned move happened.
